payload.name: Extract_Multiple_Facts_Per_Message
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when a user message contains multiple distinct events, facts, or state changes; create a separate candidate for each rather than only the most salient one.
content: During candidate extraction, treat each explicit durable fact or event in a message as a separate candidate; do not let one salient topic (e.g., a trip) suppress another explicitly stated fact (e.g., a vehicle breakdown).
If a message contrasts two items or time periods (old vs new, before vs after), capture each side's state separately so that later questions can retrieve either fact.
Before finalizing a memory for a message, scan the raw text for every independent claim about the subject's possessions, plans, or experiences and ensure each is represented in some candidate.

solves: The diagnosed cause was that extraction produced one candidate from a message containing two distinct user facts: a trip and a separate breakdown of a different item, so the breakdown was never stored. The abstract failure is single-candidate dominance, where a more prominent event causes other explicit durable facts in the same message to be omitted. This rule applies to any construction session where a message bundles multiple independent facts, events, or state changes, and prevents loss of evidence needed for later questions.
